Almraiven was one of the great cities of the nation of Calimshan.[2][7][15] It was most notable for being the nation's first and premier center for magical studies,[2][7][13] earning it the moniker "City of Spells".[7][12] Following the return of the noble genies Calim and Memnon, who led genasi in overthrowing the Calimshan government, Almraiven became the only human-controlled city in the region[16] until the late 15th century DR, when the region's enslaved populace rose up and overthrew their tyrannical genie-kin rulers.[17]

“
Almraiven has never been conquered by the mad tyrants of the Elemental Chaos. Neither djinni nor efreeti has ever ruled her. No other city in these lands can make that claim.
”
— WeavePasha Acham el Jhotos.[18]

Geography[]

Almraiven was on the south-western shores of Calimshan, a port of the Shining Sea.[19][20] It was close to the Spider Swamp and Alimir Mountains.[19][20][21]

Description[]

Organization[]

Almraiven was built using the "drudach system",[7] much like nearly every other settlement throughout Calimshan.[22][23] This Calishite form of urban structuring, established all the way back to when the land was ruled by genies,[23] consisted of an interlocking series of small brick-walled neighborhoods called drudachs.[22][23] All drudachs were further grouped together into subdivisons known as sabbans, whose boundaries were similarly marked by low mud-brick walls. Each sabban worked as a self-sufficient town—it had its own water supplies, guards, markets, residences, and so on.[23] The city had a total of 12 sabbans and 49 drudachs.[7]

The largest of these sabbans was the Mage's Quarter. Located in the center of the city, it was comprised of seven drudachs.[24]

Like other port cities in Calimshan, Almraiven had piers and wharves that were specially designated for use by the navy.[25]

Government[]

For much of Calimshan's history, vizars (a title equivalent to "merchant-prince") held true power within the nation's city-states. The ruling head of the nation had no direct control over the cities that made up Calimshan. Following the rise of Syl-pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal, vizars were afforded less direct power, making the possibility of a coup like the one that had brought him to power no longer feasible. In Almraiven much like Calimport, the vizar did not directly oversee those of lesser ranking, but instead was a syl-vizar under whom other vizars handled the overseeing of Almraiven's sabbalads and druzirs.[26]

For much of the 14th century DR, the ruling vizar of Almraiven was Majel el Arpooristan. He filtered all his acts of governance through the advice and consent of a council of 15 or so of Almraiven's most powerful pashas,[8][7] with the most influential among them being Fatima el Galsah, eldest daughter of Ralan el Pesarkhal,[7][27] with even the other pashas cowtowing to her.[7] Through her and eight other loyal pashas, Syl-pasha Pesarkhal controlled almost every aspect of the city's government, trade, and underworld.[7]

In Almraiven, other vizars do not directly oversee any lessers but are syl-vizars over their fellows, allowing them to fulfill the Calishite dream of the greatest profit and ascendancy for the least effort. Their subservient vizars handle the duties of overseeing the sabbalads and druzirs.[28]

During el Djenispool Dynasty, Admiral Eshtarl Eshram held considerable influence over Majel and his council, for he was overseeing the construction of the top-secret Pasha's Palace as well as other major warships.[8]

Almost all magic and wizardry in the city were controlled and regulated by the Guild Arcane, which was lead by the Caleph Arcane. The Caleph was politically, if not magically, the most influential and powerful wizard in all of Almraiven. They wielded considerable influence over the city and among its pashas.[7] Sometime following the return of the noble genies Calim and Memnon and their dissolution of the Calimshan government,[16] the city's then caleph arcane, Acham el Jhotos, ceased power as Almraiven's new ruler.[9] Abandoning the titles of old, he went by the moniker of WeavePasha or Sultan Supreme.[14] His eldest grandchild,[29] Munaa yr Oma el Jhotos,[30] a powerful sorceress in her own right,[29] served as the High Vizar.[30]

Crime[]

Under the reign of Syl-Pasha Pesarkhal, the underworld of Calimshan was whittled down to four major crime families[31] who were inter-meshed with the government system.[7] This left the vast majority of criminal enterprises in Almraiven to fall under the purview of el Vyndahla,[7][31] though they were influenced by el Pesarkhal to do as the Syl-Pasha desires.[31] Beneath them were the minor criminal families el Ahimar, el Beza, el Efead, el Haedi, el Moadyph, el Tamoah,[3] and el Skahil.[32]

El Vyndahla was allied with the criminal consortium Rundeen,[31] who for a time had control over both Almraiven and all trade on the southern coast of the Shining Sea. Their monopoly was shattered in the years following the reunification of Calishite cities under Syl-Pasha Pesarkhal.[33][34] Together the two organizations controlled most of the piracy and smuggling in Calimshan, though tempered by el Pesarkhal to not cause a total disruption of shipping and trade into and out of the nation.[31] The Rundeen-affiliated thieves' guild Many Long Arms were also based in Almraiven.[35]

Through their agent Shangalar the Black, the Rundeen controlled most of the city's minor crime families. They either owned or sponsored half of Almraiven's shipbuilders, ensuring them cheap labor and lumber from the likes of Lapaliiya, the Shaar, and Tashalar. And almost all of the pashas of Almraiven's cooper, farrier, moneylender, saddler, and shipwright guilds were full members of the Rundeen. The government taxes and fees of these pashas were paid on their behalf by the Rundeen, acting as a bribe to the city's vizars that encouraged patronage of Rundeen-run concerns.[36] By 1370 DR, el Vyndahla was plotting with the Rundeen to loosen or even break the stranglehold that el Pesarkhal had over the Calimshan underworld. All the while, Syl-Pasha Pesarkhal was also plotting, waiting until his forces and alliances were in just the right place to eliminate the traitorous crime family altogether.[31]

Despite all of this talk of the Rundeen's influence, the biggest power player in the Almraivenar underworld during this time was Pasha Jafar el Limiz. His sole official claim to power was having majority control of the largest non-Rundeen shipbuilding business in the city, though he also had numerous shrewd alliances and an illicit relationship with Fatima el Galsah. Among the minor crime families of Almraiven he was variously considered an ally, a respected enemy, and a superior.[3]

Trade[]

This port city did not rely upon any one particular industry for trade, though it did shine in two particular industries. Firstly, all manner of magic items were produced in Almraiven,[1] though usually craftsmen focused on making the more common, less-powerful magic items.[1][7] The likes of potions, wands, and lesser frivolities.[7] This was due to such items being quicker to produce and overall more affordable. The city's craftsmen of magic items roused complaints from competitors in other Calishite cities, condemning them as "flooding the market", but local merchants paid them no heed.[1] Its status as a center of magic also made stock of raw spell components rather limited amongst apothecaries, herbalists, and black marketeers.[24]

Almraiven's other claim to fame was being a major center of shipbuilding,[1][7] as well as ship supplies,[7] boasting one of the largest facilities in Calimshan.[2][7] This status became even more prominent following the establishment of the Qysanallojal, Calimshan's navy. Due to being the farthest port from the Sea of Swords, it was the hub of the nation's most ambitious and secret naval projects. In 1357 DR, Almraiven's shipbuilders were hard at work crafting the ambitious Pasha's Palace, one of the largest warships in Faerûnian history. The city's shipyards were all set to start production of five more following sea trials,[1] however, on its maiden voyage in 1360 DR the Pasha's Palace was sunken by a kraken.[37]

Other less industries of note included textiles, such as carpet weaving.[7] Together these industries offset the heavy costs the Almraiven had for food importation, having to rely upon such trade as the land surrounding the city was nonarable. Its large docks were primarily built with this in mind, making them perfect for large grain-hauling ships and other bulk food carriers to make port.[1]

Altogether the festhalls, inns, and taverns of Memnon numbered around 600 or so. Due to city statues put in place all the way back during the Shoon Imperium, wizards were not allowed to own nor work at these sorts of entertainment venues, for fear that they would come to dominate all aspects of Almraivenar life.[24] Additionally, like many cities in Calimshan, Almraiven's tavern landscape was dominated by Golden Sands affiliated taverns. These were denoted by having either "Golden" or "Sands" in their name.[38]

During the Fourth and Fifth Ages of Calimshan, the aranea of the neighboring Spider Swamp traded in herbs, poisons, and silk with the people of Almraiven. Trade relations lulled in the centuries following Shoon V scapegoating them as the cause of the Alley Plague, but eventually aranea manged to establish new small trade agreements under the cover of the Silverstars Trading Coster.[39][note 3]

Throughout much of Calimshan's history,[40] save for the Seventh Age when Mameluks ruled in,[41] slavery was a common institution in the nation and its city-states,[40] including the likes of Almraiven.[42]

Under the reign of WeavePasha Acham, the institution of slavery continued in Almraiven[43] and the city's trade policy focused on forging ties with other seafaring nations.[13] Slaves grew food, fished, produced clothing, cleaned the city's streets, and even acted as its defenders. However, unbeknownst to many Almraivenar, the WeavePasha had ambitions of abolishing the institution altogether.[43] To this end, the city's slaves lived under much lighter restrictions than elsewhere in the Skyfire Emirates. They were able to form communities, keep familial relations active even when kin were separated, and maintained a culture coherent enough to support a shadow economy. Rather than coin, the people dealt in information and rumors, doing a great deal of trade with the Janessar,[44] a secret society of abolitionists that covertly worked with the WeavePasha.[45][note 4] The principal agent of the Janessar within Almraiven during this time was a gnoll by the name of T'Emma.[44]

Defenses[]

Law & Order[]

In 1370 DR, around 1050 amlakkar were stationed in Almraiven, with 75 officers across each drudach. There was also a contingent of 400 soldiers and 30 junior and senior officers.[24]

The city had significant naval forces, counted as being amongst the highest of the Calishite cities. On average there were no fewer than 30 ships moored in Almraiven at any given time.[25] Among the naval ships and the city's support services, there were nearly nearly 600 officers and sailors on duty.[24]

Under the reign of the WeavePasha Acham, many slaves served within the city's militia and filled out the lowest ranks of the amlakkar.[43]

Culture[]

Almraiven was a very cosmopolitan metropolis, filled with a great variety of diversity.[1]

The city was particularly famed among wizards and sorcerers as being a premiere center of magical study, a history dating all the way back to the Sixth or Fifth Age of Calimshan,[2][7][46][24][47][note 5] when its first school of magic was established.[46] Though some would claim it had held that prestige since ever further back, all the way in the Third Age.[2][7][46][24][47][note 5] The ability to wield magic was a major factor in acquiring and holding any sort of power in Almraiven. Even visiting foreign wizards could garner some measure of respect. However, many regard the city's reputation as a place of power as merely Calishite arrogance, rather than any sort of special quality in the local Weave.[24]

Currency[]

Dating back to the Eighth Age of Calimshan,[48] all coinage in major cities like Almraiven were minted separately to different designs and referred to by different names than similar denominations in other major cities of Calimshan,[1][48] with their only unifying feature being the "Pasha's mark", which certified a coin's value.[1] An exception to this was the cities of Almraiven and Volothamp, whom used all the same names for their coin denominations, although the cities used different slang.[48] Under Syl-Pasha Pesarkhal, who met resistance from his pashas and vizars on changing the country's monetary system, the shape of coins across all of the major cities was standardized. From then on copper and silver coins were triangular, gold and electrum coins were circular, and coins forged of platinum were square.[48]

The coin denominations of Almraiven were as follows
  • Copper pieces were known locally as "rada",[1][48] but were referred to in slang as "river".[48]
  • Electrum pieces were known locally as "tazo",[1][48] but were referred to in slang as "tear".[48]
  • Gold pieces were known locally as "rekatik", but were referred to in slang as "sun".[48]
  • Platinum pieces were known locally as "mandrille", but were referred to in slang as "star".[48]
  • Silver pieces were known locally as "espedrille", but were referred to in slang as "moon".[48]

Events & Festivals[]

In the wake of the loss of their genie leaders in 1450 DR,[13] factions from the cities of Calimport and Memnon came together with leaders from Almraiven to organize a race across the Calim Desert,[49][note 6][note 7] starting at an oasis somewhere between Calimport and Memnon.[50] To the champion of this race would be afforded a large gem referred to as the "Heart of the Desert". This race went on to become a triennial event among the three cities, each time with the ultimate prize being the largest gem found in the prior three years.[49]

Religions[]

There about nearly twice as many churches and temples in Almraiven as there were drudachs. The majority of these were dedicated to deities of either magic or the sea, such as Azuth, Istishia,[3] Mystra,[4] and Umberlee.[6][3] and Though there were was also some presence of Talona worship.[5]

Inhabitants[]

The bulk of Almraiven's populace was made up of humans. Beyond them there were a prominent number of half-elves living in the city. Those who made up the miscellaneous "others" portion of the population[7] included various types of humanoids,[42] such as gnolls[44][42] and flinds, who were purchased on their way to the Alimir Mountains to work as galley slaves or work for a wage in mercenary companies.[42]

History[]

The city was founded in the the −6000 DR as part of eastern Coramshan.[10][11][12][note 1] Over the centuries it would be besieged by all manner of foes, including at one point dragons.[18][note 8]

Circa −4900 DR, the cities of Almraiven and Calimport were hit by the Warriors' Plague.[51]

Calimshan Empire[]

In −790 DR, the Calimshan Empire became embroiled in the first of a series of conflicts with the drow[52][53] of Guallidurth,[53] later dubbed collectively as the Night Wars.[52][53] In the Year of Furious Giants, −697 DR, the drow erupted from beneath Almraiven, as well as the cities of Calimport and Manshaka, establishing footholds within them and their outlying wilderness. They would maintain these footholds for the next several decades.[52][54]

In −676 DR, Almraiven was among the cities struck by the Temples Plague.[55]

In the Year of Gilded Burials, −187 DR, following the Throne Wars of Calimshan, the Syl-Pasha Tasyn el Tarshaj yi Manshaka and his family simultaneously conquered the cities of Almraiven, Calimport, Manshaka, and Memnon, unifying the Pasha's Lands.[56][57]

In the Fifth Age of Calimshan,[46] beginning in the Year of Many Eyes, −170 DR, the Lands of Intrigue became embroiled in the Eye Tyrant Wars.[46][58] Within the first three months of the conflict, the city of Almraiven fell to the beholders of the Alimir Hive and by the end of Kythorn they had conquered the neighboring Spider Swamp. By −166 DR the Eye Tyrant Wars came to an end, restoring human rule to Almraiven.[58][59]

Also during this era, an influential family known as the Pehrri owned most of the city's largest shipbuilders. Their whole clan, save for Florian Perry and his wife, would go on to be assassinated by the the syl-pasha under the accordances of Florian's desire for revenge against the family for the injustices they had dealt to his grandfather.[46]

In the Year of the Choking Spores, −52 DR, Almraiven was among the cities struck by the Flower Plague.[58]

Shoon Imperium[]

Over the course of the Shoon Imperium, the Guilds Arcane were established by the ruling Qysars. The very first of these to be established would be that of Almraiven.[7]

In the Year of Dark Venom, 37 DR, with Umberlant worship waning among Calishites after more than a century of peaceful waters, five massive waves struck at different points across the Shoon Imperium. The cities of Almraiven, Manshaka, Teshburl,[6] Memnon, and Calimport.[60] About a third to two-thirds of each settlement was severely damaged by flooding. Through this terror Umberlee inspired renewed reverence among the Calishites. Since that day, Memnon was never without at least two structures dedicated to Umberlee, for fear that lack of reverence would bring the "Vengeance Waves" to bear upon them once more.[6]

In 39 DR, Almraiven was once more stricken by disease, that of the Alley Plague, but it was restricted to the city's docks.[61] In the Year of Full Cribs, 290 DR, another plague ravaged Almraiven.[39][62] On this occasion, it accidentally unleashed by Qysara Shoon V. Needing a scapegoat,[39] the ruler cast blame upon the neighboring aranea of Spider Swamp, leading to a devastating backlash from the military and civilian populace of Volothamp.[39][62] One of Shoon V's daughters, Selara, went on to marry Almraiven's Caleph Arcane at the time, Nadim el Jhotos.[63]

In 138 DR, Almraiven is among a number of cities in the Shoon Imperium to suffer great fires within its poorer, wooden sections. While likely the result of fireworks that the Qysar had demanded for his birthday, Qsar Amahl Shoon IV blamed the incidences on the Church of Ilmater.[64]

In 204 DR, a gladiator-slave by the name of Harakti broke free from a minor fighting arena in Almraiven and built up an army of fellow embittered slaves and disenfranchised freemen, beginning the Harakhti Uprisings. That same year, Qysar Amahl Shoon IV peacefully passed away, leaving his grandson Shoon VI to take the throne.[65]

In 319 DR,[66] with rates of crime and violence increasing across the Shoon Imperium,[67] Qysar Shoon VII decided to take drastic measures. He ordered oil to be poured into the sewers of major imperial cities, causing the Great Fires.[66][67] While originally planned to be controlled blazes, the fires raged almost unchecked. With a death toll reaching over three million people,[67] or 43% of the population, the cities of Almraiven,[66] Ankhapur, Calimport, Innarlith, Ithmong, and Memnon were near completely devastated.[67]

Calimshan[]

In the Year of the Sad Refrains, 733 DR, a secret society known as the Rundeen make a power play to usurp Calimshan's supremacy over trade in the southern Sword Coast. Ships flying false colors sailed into the ports of Almraiven and Calimport, then once they had docked at a place close to shore and deeply entrenched among other ships they were magically exploded. Posthumously referred to as the "Port Fires" incident, fires engulfed the docks, shipyards, and port-facing warehouses in Almraiven, claiming the lives of 18% of its populace.[68]

In the Year of the Enigma, 755 DR, a magical plague ravaged many cities across Calimshan, including Almraiven. On average, each of the cities affected suffered a 16% loss of their populace.[68]

During the Eighth Age of Calimshan, from the 1140's to 1180's DR, a series of trade wars were tearing the nation's city-states apart. In 1187 DR, a sabbalad in Almraiven by the name of Saban el Djenispool decided to take matters into his own hands to save the nation, using his secret a network of enforcers and spies to set about building a coup. By Higharvestide of that year, Saban entered Calimport and slaughtered any troublesome pasha that posed resistant to him. He decreed, "Accept me as syl-pasha over all the city-states of Calimshan, and peace and free trade will be restored. Resist, and feel the might of my army." By the end of 1187 DR, the nation was once more unified, beginning the Djenispool Dynasty.[69]

In 1370 DR, in the month of Hammer, a number of trade ships from Zakhara arrive to Almraiven, provoking a frenzy of activity in the city's bazaars and marketplaces. Amidst this mercantile frenzy were rumors of djinni bottles having been smuggled into the country alongside a shipment of metalwork and rare carpets. The Guild Arcane impounded the cargo of the alleged culprit vessel, the Golden Voyager, and had its whole crew arrested. A few days later, against the wishes of the Caleph Arcane, curious amlakkar opened the suspected djinni bottles. A strange pungent mist arose from the containers, clinging to them like claws described "as cold as ice". In a panic the rest of the amlakkar threw their bottles against the wall of their minaret. Olive green mists billowed forth from the shattered bottles, filling the municipal tower, before wafting out into the city.[70]

Initially there were no noticeable effects from the olive mists beyond a slight chill, but over the course of three weeks,[70] passing into the month of Alturiak, those exposed were found to spontaneously combusting when in heightened emotional states or in the midst of strenuous activity. All incidinces were reported as occuring within Almraiven's four western sabbans, those that were along the waterfront and the lower sections of the city. Labeled the Bottlemist Plague, many began fleeing the city that month in fear of catching it themselves. Syl-Pasha Pesarkhal, who was on route to the city that month, received word of the Bottlemist Plague and shifted course to the city of Volothamp, wherein he then demanded an audience with Almraiven's Caleph Arcane.[71]

By the month of Ches, more than 4000 people were reported dead from the Bottlemist Plague and Almraiven was left largely deserted. Ilmatari clergy and laymens make their way to the city, intent on alleviating the suffering and putting an end to the plague. By Tarsakh the Bottlemist Plague had largely run its course, with the Ilmatari managing to save a few of its sufferers. Those less fortunate combusted within their homes, setting fire to large sections of the city's docks and lower sabbans.[71]

That same year, prominent leader Fatima el Galsah's husband was kidnapped and sold into slavery to the Alimir Hive. She accused a prominent Rundeen trader, Kyahj el Haedi, of engineering the situation and held senior members of el Vyndahla accountable. Rumors proceeded to rumble rampantly of a coming underworld war on Almraiven's streets.[27]

Post-Spellplague[]

After the Spellplague of the Year of Blue Fire, 1385 DR, the High Magic that bound Calim and Memnon in the Calimemnon Crystal shattered, unleashing them upon the world. Freed, the two genies resumed their millennia-old hostilities,[13][72][73] In the wake of the return of Calim and Memnon, many of the residents of Calimshan, presumed to be human, manifested their genasi heritage. These descendants of the elemental powers pledged themselves to either elemental air or fire, the forces of Calim and Memnon respectively.[13] With the aid of their loyal genasi, the two genies overthrew the Calimshan government[13][74] and ushered in the Second Era of Skyfire.[74][73] Those humans who fled from conflict made their way to Almraiven.[74]

Almraiven was fortunate enough to go relatively undamaged by the chaotic effects the Spellplague caused in much of the land. Consequently, this left the city's mages in a good position to fend off attacks from genasi when they waged their rebellion against the Calishite state.[13] With the land absent of governance, Almraiven's then Caleph Arcane, Acham el Jhotos,[9] a mage whose family was secretly descended from Qysara Shoon the Fifth,[75] ceased power and took on the title of WeavePasha.[9] He would swear to defend his city against the endless wars of air and fire.[13] Alongside the other Almraivenar spellcasters, he managed the city with great acumen and wisdom,[74] though with a tenuous grasp on maintaining peace.[13]

Ambitiously envisioning an Almraiven that would live up to being a shining exemplar of "human" achievement, the WeavePasha endeavored to one day completely rewrite all aspects of Calishite society that composed the city. Government structures, social structures, the ways of doing business, the institutions of faith, the institutions of magic, and the institution of slavery–in the eyes of Acham, all these things were descended from Memnonnar society and thus were the influence of djinni, not humans.[43] Referring to his grand restructuring project as "human husbandry", the WeavePasha laid out nested plans with timelines running into the centuries.[76]

During this tumultuous period, the Janessar abolitionists would direct any slaves they freed to the city of Almraiven.[77] The WeavePasha would also occasionally sends agitators and expatriates of Akanûl to stir up trouble in either of the genasi-controlled city-states, to which he would then feign ignorance and use their rival as a scapegoat.[13]

In 1479 DR, the WeavePasha ordered a fleet of long, deep carracks to be built within the city's renowned shipyards.[13] The construction of this fleet was to be overseen by some of his sons.[78] Many speculated as to the purpose of these vessels, with some saying they were to going to be used in a coming naval raid on Calimport. Others would theorize they were be built in case of evacuation, though the fleet would have only been capable of carrying about one-tenth of Almraiven's population at the time.[13]

Notable Locations[]

Amphitheater of Tasryn
A huge amphitheater near the center of the city that in centuries past was once an Ishtisian temple.[3]
Arcane Alcazar
A college of magic that was established by the WeavePasha.[79]
Brothers' Arcane School of Magic
A school of arcane learning where both secular and ecclesiastical Azuthan magic were taught.[3]
El Jhotos's Palace
This lavish palace was heavily warded and contained large gardens with trees similar to those that grew in the Forest of Mir prior to the Spellplague.[80]
The Familiar
An expensive festhall in the Mage's Quarter that was largely patroned by spellcasters.[24]
The First Chosen's Hall
A garrison turned Azuthan temple and monastery.[3]
Imaskars' House
An elegant festhall and inn.[24]
The Qysar's Cups
An affordable tavern whose staff dressed in an ancient Shoonite fashion.[24]
School of Arcane Hands
The city's first ever school of magical study.[24]
Shining Scimitars
A tavern that was owned and operated in the 14th century DR by an adventuring company[24][35] known as the Scimitars of Mullivan.[35]
Street of Stolen Stones
A street within a warehouse district of the city. In 1479 DR, a group of conjurers tracking down Corvus Nightfeather on behalf of the WeavePasha summoned a chain of runespiral demons after they felt their spectral hounds had caught his scent near the city docks.[78]
T'Emma's Bar
A divebar located in a basement near the docks that was operated by T'Emma, the Janessar's principal agent within the city. It was a valuable source of information for those who dealt in seedier lines of work.[44]
The Trident Towers
A major Umberlant temple.[3]
Yulthaari Shipyards
A shipyard that was controlled by the Rundeen.[81]

  3. ↑ Since the book dates the habitation of aranea in the Spider Swamp as following the Night Wars, then the commerce they developed within a few centuries had to have occurred during the Fourth & Fifth Ages of Calimshan.
  4. ↑ The organized play module Heart of the Desert seemed to be written under the impression that slavery was not an active institution in Almraiven. To the authors' credit, such a thing was not stated about the city during 4th edition outside of the novel Sandstorm. However, since that novel also portrays the WeavePasha as being in opposition to slavery and wishing to bring it to an end, it would still make sense that the Janessar are working with him as stated in Heart of the Desert.
  5. ↑ 5.0 5.1 Both Empires of the Shining Sea on page 101 of its text and Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting state that Almraiven has held its role as a premiere center of magical study for "over 3000 years". Taking into account the Present date for the former, that would put it at around the -1600's DR, what Calimport (1998) (page 12) labels as the Third Age of Calimshan. On page 102, Empires of the Shining Sea adds that "The Guild Arcane of Almraiven established the School of Arcane Hands more than three millennia ago".

    However, page 101 also states that the Guilds Arcane were established during the Shoon Imperium, which was the Sixth Age of Calimshan (27 DR-450 DR). And on page 20 the book states that during the Fifth Age "...mages were becoming more prevalent and their craft more accessible to pursue, as evidenced in the construction of the first Calishite school of magic in Almraiven." Taken together, this information throws into question the validity of the supposed "three millennia" of mystic prestige.
  6. ↑ Unless otherwise stated, all Forgotten Realms content released as part of 4th edition Dungeons & Dragons is assumed to take place in 1479 DR.
  7. ↑ The adventure refers to this race tradition as having been going on "for the past 30 years." Since the date of the adventure is assumed to be 1479 DR, it more likely began in the year when the Second Era of Skyfire came to an end, 1450 DR.
  8. ↑ The novel Sandstorm mentions offhandedly that over the centuries Almraiven had been "conquered by human armies and dragons", but without any greater context it's impossible to place this information within the context of a timeline.
